summary:
Our project aims to create an interactive Martian map that helps future explorers understand the challenges of surviving on Mars. It presents important information about the planet's surface, potential exploration areas, environmental conditions, and possible risks that astronauts may face.

By organizing relevant planetary information into a simple and accessible guide, our solution can help users explore Mars and better understand what it takes to establish a human presence there.

This project is important because future human missions to Mars will require careful planning, reliable information, and a clear understanding of the environment. Our goal is to make Martian exploration more accessible, educational, and engaging through technology and interactive visualization.
details:
Martian Map is a proposed interactive mapping solution designed to help future astronauts and researchers explore the surface of Mars.

The concept focuses on combining different types of planetary information, such as surface imagery, elevation, terrain features, and geological data, into one easy-to-understand map. Users would be able to explore regions, compare map layers, identify points of scientific interest, and evaluate possible exploration routes.

The intended benefits include making Mars data easier to understand, supporting mission planning, and helping explorers consider terrain challenges before choosing a route.

Our concept is inspired by the need for safer and more informed human exploration of Mars. Its creative aspect is bringing different scientific perspectives together in one accessible interface.

For the proposed prototype, we plan to use NASA and USGS open datasets, HTML, CSS, JavaScript, and mapping and visualization tools. The design considers data reliability, usability, accessibility, and the limitations of future Mars missions.

The project is currently at the concept stage, with the goal of developing it into a functional interactive prototype.
